decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up left-arm approach; coin is near the center-left, so use left arm without crossing. Shape wrist downward before translating toward holder.
Back off the wrist shaping after continuity rejection; restore a neutral pose before a downward elbow-up approach.
Tilt left wrist toward a downward pinch with small continuous increments; keep right arm parked.
Continue elbow-up wrist rotation and move inward above the bank toward the coin; hold generous vertical clearance.
Replan from interrupted pose with smaller rotations, lifting and moving toward the center-left holder while staying clear of the bank.
Advance above the holder and continue the downward pinch orientation with elbow-up continuity; bank remains to the left of the approach.
Continue toward coin from the left at clearance height, incrementally finishing the vertical approach orientation.
Center the downward gripper above the coin using the head and wrist views; maintain clearance before lowering.
Lower toward the coin while yaw-aligning the jaws to its visible plane; open gripper until the coin is at pinch depth.
Correct wrist yaw from visual feedback and offset the pinch toward the coin center; descend only a small amount while refining alignment.
Coin is centered between the jaws in the wrist view. Make a millimetric depth/yaw correction and begin closing around its exposed rim.
Finish closing on the coin and make a short test lift. Retention will be checked from its separation from the holder, not the gripper command.
Lift vertically with the gripper fully closed to clear the holder and inspect whether the coin follows.
The coin is no longer retained and is visibly on the table just right of center. Clear the left arm and begin an elbow-up right-arm recovery approach to the coin.
Clear space for recovery. Continue right-arm downward shaping and move inward; coin has settled farther toward the robot after falling.
Move the right gripper above the fallen coin with small continuous downward-wrist increments; left stays clear.
Continue right-arm approach above the coin, finishing the vertical wrist orientation before lowering to table level.
Center the right downward gripper over the flat coin using the calibrated head view, then inspect wrist alignment before pinching.
Use a small diagonal correction and descent to bring the flat coin toward the pinch center; inspect its motion in the wrist view before closing.
Correct the lateral wrist-image error toward the flat coin center and lower gently, keeping the jaws open for an edge pinch.
Coin shifted left during the low approach. Lift the right gripper clear of the table and bring the left gripper above the new location without dragging the jaws.
The coin has settled on the left. Align the left wrist laterally above it and descend only to clearance height; withdraw the right arm sideways.
Center the flat coin beneath the left pinch axis using wrist-image errors while staying above contact height; keep the right arm clear.
Coin is nearly centered. Descend vertically with a small optical correction and narrow the jaws, stopping above the table before final edge contact.
Correct the coin's downward wrist-image offset before contacting it; approach the rim slowly with narrower jaws and no broad lateral sweep.
Visual feedback shows the last correction moved away from the coin. Lift before repositioning, then shift above its center using the observed image-motion direction.
Coin is now centered at the pinch axis. Descend vertically in small increments with the jaws spaced outside the disk, keeping lateral correction minimal.
Close slowly around the flat coin's rim at table height, with only a few millimeters of descent and a slight lateral centering correction.
Maintain full closure to let the rim pinch settle, then test a short vertical lift and inspect retention.
Continue a slow vertical retention test with full closure; the coin rim is visible but secure capture remains uncertain.
Coin stayed on the table during the lift. Reopen above it and correct the small lateral offset while lowering vertically for a more centered rim pinch.
Coin center now aligns with the pinch point. Lower a few millimeters to rim level and close symmetrically without lateral motion.
The disk is now visibly between the separated closed-command jaws. Test retention with a slow vertical lift while maintaining full closure.
The flat coin slipped from the shallow rim contact. Reopen and approach more deeply straight down, avoiding lateral sweeps, so the jaw sides can contact its edge.
Close symmetrically at the deeper rim-contact height and hold steady before any lift.
Test the deeper edge capture with a gentle vertical lift while keeping full closure; inspect the coin relative to the jaws and tabletop.
The coin remains on the table. Recenter above its shifted position with clearance, rather than repeating the same off-center pinch.
The coin's near rim now lies at the jaw tips instead of behind them. Close gradually on that rim with a shallow vertical descent.
The rim visibly separates the closed-command jaws. Lift slowly to check whether this capture is retained.
The shallow pinch slipped. Approach the flat disk vertically to a lower rim-contact height with jaws open outside its diameter, avoiding lateral pushing.
Stop downward motion at the observed contact height. Close slowly and symmetrically around the centered disk without pressing farther into the tabletop.
Let the centered edge pinch settle at full closure, then lift only a centimeter to check for secure retention.
The coin now stays fixed between the jaws during the test lift. Raise it clear of the table while maintaining full closure before reorienting for the bank slot.
Retained coin is lifted clear. Begin transport toward the left bank and rotate the disk from flat toward vertical, keeping closure and gradual elbow-up motion.
Continue the supported rotation and transport toward the bank with the coin visibly fixed in the jaws. Keep the disk clear of the bank while changing its plane.
Bring the held disk toward a vertical plane matching the bank slot, with clearance above the bank. Continue gradual rotation and left-workspace transport.
The prior chunk executed no movement due to continuity limits. Replan with reduced translation and rotation while preserving the coin grasp.
Reduce wrist increments again after the guard interruption. Continue toward slot alignment while lowering slightly from the high transport pose.
Continue rotating the retained coin upright, translating toward the slot while preserving clearance and smooth joint changes.
Finish bringing the disk upright and approach above the slot. Keep closure, using small descent increments until the slot alignment can be refined visually.
Disk is upright and retained. Descend toward the slot while correcting the head-view alignment, keeping small increments and monitoring arm continuity.
Refine the coin's vertical projection over the slot with millimetric lateral corrections. Limit descent near the arm's near-neutral configuration instead of folding the elbow downward.
The slot is visible directly below the upright coin. Correct the small wrist-view lateral offset, settle, and release symmetrically over the slot without forcing a downward elbow fold.
Hold alignment and open fully, allowing the release to occur before withdrawing. Observe the coin rather than relying on the reported gripper command.
Coin has landed at the slot. Allow it to settle while gently withdrawing the open left gripper and beginning the right arm's continuous return toward origin.
The coin has disappeared through the slot in RGB. Complete the left arm's return to origin and continue the right arm's elbow-up return, with both grippers open.
Settle the left arm at its origin and continue the right arm's smooth retraction and wrist restoration; the bank slot remains clear after the coin release.
Continue returning the right arm to its original pose with progressively smaller translations and continuous elbow-up joint motion.
